evidence.label: A Gepner stability condition on every smooth quintic threefold
Prescribed large-volume charges on threefolds with trivial canonical bundle

headline: A stability condition on every smooth quintic threefold with Toda’s exact 2/5 Gepner symmetry.
scope: Every smooth complex quintic threefold; and, separately, every smooth projective complex threefold with trivial canonical bundle at large volume.
plain: A stability condition sorts the objects of an algebraic category by an angle called phase. Toda conjectured that every smooth quintic threefold has one with a special symmetry that raises every phase by exactly 2/5. The first paper claims to construct it. The second claims the exact large-volume charges on every threefold with trivial canonical bundle. It also claims a uniform version of a key inequality for every smooth projective threefold.
doesNot: This does not describe the whole space of stability conditions or give the large-volume charges at small volume.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Y. Toda, who stated the normalized quintic Gepner conjecture
scorecard.significanceWhy: If correct, it settles a named conjecture on the quintic and supplies exact large-volume stability on Calabi–Yau threefolds.

explanation:
Picture a clock face with five equal marks. A turn by one mark is a rotation by one fifth of a full circle. In complex numbers that turn is multiplication by e^(2πi/5). Five such turns bring you back to the start, because e^(2πi) = 1. This small fact sits at the centre of the first paper.

A stability condition sorts the objects of a derived category, an algebraic record of all sheaves on a space. It assigns each object a complex number called its central charge. The angle of that number, measured in half turns, is the object’s phase. Semistable objects are the basic pieces, and every object must split into finitely many of them in order of phase. Bridgeland gave the mathematical framework for this idea in 2007[1].

The space here is a quintic threefold, the set where one degree-five equation in five variables vanishes. It is a standard Calabi–Yau threefold, a three-dimensional complex shape with trivial canonical bundle. On it there is a special symmetry Φ of the derived category. Doing Φ five times equals shifting by 2[3]. A Gepner point is a stability condition that this symmetry rotates. Toda gave the precise quintic conjecture in 2013[2].

The first paper claims to prove Toda’s conjecture for every smooth complex quintic threefold[2,4]. Its stability condition is turned by Φ: every central charge is multiplied by e^(2πi/5). The symmetry Φ also raises every phase by exactly 2/5[4]. The numbers fit together. Five steps of 2/5 make 2, matching the shift by 2. Five rotations by e^(2πi/5) give 1, and a shift by 2 also leaves the charge unchanged. A point of the threefold has charge −1, which is phase 1, half a turn[4].

Stability conditions on every smooth quintic were already known to exist, by work of Li[5]. What was missing was one with this exact symmetry[5]. Toda had already proposed the right two-step construction, called a double tilt. He flagged one remaining difficulty[6]. The Gepner charge involves irrational numbers, so its values need not form a discrete grid. Then it is hard to show that splitting into semistable pieces stops after finitely many steps[6]. The paper’s central step keeps two independent small adjustments of Toda’s construction. Together they bound the numerical size of semistable objects before those objects are even defined[7]. That bound makes the splitting finite.

The second paper treats a wider class of spaces. It covers every smooth projective complex threefold with trivial canonical bundle[8]. There, physics predicts central charges for large volume, meaning a large size parameter t. The paper claims stability conditions with exactly those charges at every large enough volume. This includes the ordinary charge and a version corrected by the square root of the Todd class[8]. One volume threshold works on a whole open region of parameters[9]. Earlier, Bayer’s polynomial stability gave these charges only as a limit of ever-larger volumes[10]. The new result works at each finite volume[10].

The second paper also proves a separate inequality on every smooth projective threefold. It bounds the third Chern character of tilt-semistable objects, with a fixed correction term[11]. Beyond a volume threshold the correction can be dropped[11]. This answers questions of Bernardara, Macrì, Schmidt and Zhao, and of Martinez and Schmidt[12]. The uncorrected inequality is false at some small volumes, as earlier examples show[13]. One more check on the numbers: with t = √3·a, a coefficient of a²/6 becomes t²/18, as the paper states[14].

How sure is this? No Lean formalization is listed for these papers in the openai/math release. So no computer proof checker has checked them. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Solid if both proofs hold. No Lean formalization is listed and no specialist review is published. The quintic result depends on a cited inequality of Xu.

glossary.meaning: An algebraic record of all sheaves on a space and the maps between them.
A way to sort objects of a derived category by a complex number and an angle called phase.
The complex number a stability condition assigns to each object.
The angle of the central charge, measured in half turns.
The three-dimensional set where one degree-five equation in five projective variables vanishes.
A three-dimensional complex shape whose canonical bundle is trivial.
A stability condition rotated by a special symmetry of the category by a fixed phase amount.

claims.text: Bridgeland gave the framework; stability conditions organize objects by central charge and phase with finite filtrations.
claims.sourceLine: Bridgeland gave the mathematical framework used here
claims.sourceQuote: Their physical antecedent is Douglas's proposal of $\Pi$-stability for D-branes \cite{Douglas2001}; Bridgeland gave the mathematical framework used here \cite{Bridgeland2007}.

claims.text: Toda gave the normalized quintic formulation; the theorem positively resolves this quintic conjecture.
claims.sourceLine: The following theorem positively resolves this quintic conjecture.
claims.sourceQuote: The following theorem positively resolves this quintic conjecture.

claims.text: The functor relation Φ^5 ≃ [2] is an established feature of the quintic Gepner problem.
claims.sourceLine: and its eigencharge are established features of the quintic Gepner problem
claims.sourceQuote: The functor relation $\Phi^5\simeq[2]$ and its eigencharge are established features of the quintic Gepner problem.

claims.text: Every smooth quintic admits a numerical stability condition with Z(ΦE) = e^{2πi/5}Z(E), Φ shifting phases by 2/5, and Z(O_x) = −1.
claims.sourceLine: Every smooth complex quintic threefold admits a numerical Bridgeland stability
claims.sourceQuote: Every smooth complex quintic threefold admits a numerical Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma=(Z,\mathcal P)$ with the support property on $\Knum(X)_{\R}$ such that, for every $E\in\D$ and $\varphi\in\R$, \[ Z(\Phi E)=e^{2\pi i/5}Z(E),\qquad \Phi\bigl(\mathcal P(\varphi)\bigr)=\mathcal P(\varphi+2/5),\qquad Z(\OO_x)=-1 \] for every closed point $x\in X$.

claims.text: Li established existence of numerical stability conditions on every smooth quintic; the theorem adds the Gepner symmetry.
claims.sourceQuote: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} adds the specified Gepner symmetry.

claims.text: Toda proposed the double tilt and identified Harder–Narasimhan filtrations for the irrational charge as a remaining difficulty.
claims.sourceLine: for this irrational charge as a remaining difficulty.
claims.sourceQuote: His Remark~3.10 identifies the existence of Harder--Narasimhan filtrations for this irrational charge as a remaining difficulty.

claims.text: The central step retains two independent perturbations of Toda's second cut, giving a support estimate before defining semistable objects.
claims.sourceLine: The central step is to retain two independent perturbations of Toda's second cut.
claims.sourceQuote: The central step is to retain two independent perturbations of Toda's second cut.

claims.text: On every smooth projective threefold with trivial canonical bundle, stability conditions exist with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd large-volume charges.
claims.sourceLine: We construct stability conditions with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd large-volume charges on every smooth projective complex threefold with trivial canonical bundle.
claims.sourceQuote: We construct stability conditions with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd large-volume charges on every smooth projective complex threefold with trivial canonical bundle.

claims.text: A strong tilt inequality holds on every smooth projective threefold with a fixed correction, vanishing beyond a threshold.

claims.sourceQuote: An independent argument proves strong tilt inequalities on every smooth projective complex threefold: a fixed rational correction works at every volume, and the correction vanishes beyond a threshold independent of the object and of the twist along a fixed polarization.
